records.source: Καὶ ἦλθεν εἷς ἐκ τῶν ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλων τῶν ἐχόντων τὰς ἑπτὰ φιάλας, καὶ ἐλάλησεν μετ’ ἐμοῦ λέγων· Δεῦρο, δείξω σοι τὸ κρίμα τῆς πόρνης τῆς μεγάλης τῆς καθημένης ἐπὶ ὑδάτων πολλῶν, μεθ’ ἧς ἐπόρνευσαν οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς, καὶ ἐμεθύσθησαν οἱ κατοικοῦντες τὴν γῆν ἐκ τοῦ οἴνου τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς.
records.gloss: And came one of the seven angels the having the seven bowls, and spoke with me saying: Come, I will show you the judgment of the prostitute the great the sitting on waters many, \v 2 with whom committed immorality the kings of the earth, and were made drunk those dwelling the earth from the wine of the immorality of her.
pieces: Then one of the seven angels who held the seven bowls came and spoke to me. "Come," he said, "I will show you the judgment of the great prostitute, who is seated on many waters.
With her the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality, and the people of the earth got drunk on the wine of her immorality."

L.1: And one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls came and spoke with me, saying, "Come, I will show you the judgment of the great prostitute who sits on many waters,
L.2: with whom the kings of the earth committed sexual immorality, and those who live on the earth were made drunk with the wine of her sexual immorality."

R.1: One of the seven angels who had the seven bowls came and talked with me. He said, "Come, I will show you how God will punish the great prostitute. She sits on many waters.
R.2: The kings of the earth committed sexual sins with her. The people of the earth got drunk on the wine of her sexual sins."

decisions.choice: the great prostitute: a city that seduces the nations
decisions.reason: Verse 18 says that the woman is the great city. The prophets called cities prostitutes when they traded with every nation and led them into idolatry and greed: Nineveh (Nahum 3:4), Tyre (Isaiah 23:15-17), and even Jerusalem when unfaithful (Ezekiel 16). The picture is of a city's corrupting power, not a statement about women.

decisions.choice: seated on many waters: Babylon on the Euphrates
decisions.reason: Jeremiah addressed Babylon as "you who dwell by many waters" (Jeremiah 51:13), the river and canals that made it rich. Verse 15 explains the waters as peoples and nations.

decisions.choice: sexual immorality with the kings: political and religious unfaithfulness
decisions.reason: The kings' "immorality" with her is their alliance with her power and trade and their share in her idolatry (18:3, 9). See the note on 14:8.

decisions.choice: judgment: the sentence passed on her
decisions.reason: κρίμα is the verdict and its punishment, told in chapters 17-18.

records.heading: The prostitute on the beast

records.source: καὶ ἀπήνεγκέν με εἰς ἔρημον ἐν πνεύματι.
records.gloss: And he carried away me into wilderness in spirit.
pieces: In the Spirit he took me away to a wilderness.

L.3: And he carried me away in [the] Spirit into a wilderness.

R.3: Then the Spirit took hold of me, and the angel carried me away to a desert.

decisions.choice: carried away in the Spirit: a new vision
decisions.reason: See the note on 1:10. Ezekiel was carried by the Spirit in visions (Ezekiel 3:12-14; 8:3). John is taken to a wilderness to see the prostitute, and later to a high mountain to see the bride (21:10).

decisions.choice: the Spirit took hold of me (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:10.

records.source: καὶ εἶδον γυναῖκα καθημένην ἐπὶ θηρίον κόκκινον, γέμοντα ὀνόματα βλασφημίας, ἔχων κεφαλὰς ἑπτὰ καὶ κέρατα δέκα.
records.gloss: And I saw a woman sitting on a beast scarlet, being full of names of blasphemy, having heads seven and horns ten.
pieces: I saw a woman seated on a scarlet beast. The beast was full of names that blasphemed God, and it had seven heads and ten horns.

L.3: And I saw a woman seated on a scarlet beast, full of names of blasphemy, having seven heads and ten horns.

R.3: There I saw a woman sitting on a red beast. The beast was covered with names that insulted God. It had seven heads and ten horns.

decisions.choice: the woman rides the beast: the city carried by the empire's power
decisions.reason: The beast is the one from the sea (13:1), with its heads, horns and blasphemous names. The woman is carried by it: the city's wealth and influence rest on the beast's power (17:7).

records.source: καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἦν περιβεβλημένη πορφυροῦν καὶ κόκκινον, καὶ κεχρυσωμένη χρυσίῳ καὶ λίθῳ τιμίῳ καὶ μαργαρίταις, ἔχουσα ποτήριον χρυσοῦν ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτῆς γέμον βδελυγμάτων καὶ τὰ ἀκάθαρτα τῆς πορνείας αὐτῆς, καὶ ἐπὶ τὸ μέτωπον αὐτῆς ὄνομα γεγραμμένον, μυστήριον, Βαβυλὼν ἡ μεγάλη, ἡ μήτηρ τῶν πορνῶν καὶ τῶν βδελυγμάτων τῆς γῆς.
records.gloss: And the woman was clothed in purple and scarlet, and gilded with gold and stone precious and pearls, having a cup golden in the hand of her being full of abominations and the unclean things of the immorality of her, \v 5 and on the forehead of her a name having been written, a mystery: Babylon the great, the mother of the prostitutes and of the abominations of the earth.
pieces: The woman wore purple and scarlet, and gold, precious stones, and pearls adorned her. She held a gold cup in her hand, brimming with abominations and with the uncleanness of her immorality.
On her forehead was written a name, a mystery: "Babylon the great, mother of prostitutes and of the earth's abominations."

L.4: And the woman was clothed in purple and scarlet, and adorned with gold and precious stone and pearls, holding in her hand a golden cup full of abominations and the impurities of her sexual immorality,
L.5: and on her forehead a name was written, a mystery: "Babylon the great, the mother of the prostitutes and of the abominations of the earth."

R.4: The woman wore purple and red clothes. She wore gold jewelry, precious stones, and pearls. In her hand she held a gold cup. It was full of disgusting things and of her sexual sins.
R.5: A name was written on her forehead. It was a mystery, a name with a hidden meaning: "Babylon the great, the mother of prostitutes and of all the disgusting things on the earth."

decisions.choice: purple, scarlet, gold and pearls: royal luxury
decisions.reason: Purple and scarlet dyes were costly and worn by the rich and powerful; gold, jewels and pearls are among the goods of her trade (18:12, 16). The contrast is with the bride, dressed in clean linen (19:8).

decisions.choice: abominations: idolatry and what God detests
decisions.reason: βδελυγμάτων is the word the Old Testament uses for idols and idolatrous practices (Deuteronomy 29:17; Daniel 9:27; Matthew 24:15). Her golden cup looks precious but holds what is vile (compare Jeremiah 51:7).

decisions.choice: a name on her forehead, a mystery
alternatives: "Mystery" is part of the name itself
decisions.reason: The name is written on her forehead, as God's name is on the foreheads of his people (14:1) and the beast's mark on its followers (13:16). μυστήριον most likely says that the name is to be understood in a hidden sense, as the angel explains (17:7): Babylon is not the city on the Euphrates but what it stands for.

decisions.choice: mystery; a name with a hidden meaning (R)
decisions.reason: Mystery is a key term; Readable adds what it means.

records.source: καὶ εἶδον τὴν γυναῖκα μεθύουσαν ἐκ τοῦ αἵματος τῶν ἁγίων καὶ ἐκ τοῦ αἵματος τῶν μαρτύρων Ἰησοῦ.
records.gloss: And I saw the woman being drunk from the blood of the saints and from the blood of the witnesses of Jesus.
pieces: And I saw the woman drunk on the blood of God's holy people and on the blood of Jesus's witnesses.

L.6: And I saw the woman drunk with the blood of the saints and with the blood of the witnesses of Jesus.

R.6: I saw that the woman was drunk from drinking the blood of God's people, the blood of those who told the truth about Jesus.

decisions.choice: drunk with blood: the persecution of God's people
decisions.reason: The city has killed God's people and those who bore witness to Jesus (18:24). The Roman historian Tacitus tells how Nero had Christians put to death in Rome after the fire of AD 64. μαρτύρων means witnesses; the word was coming to mean martyrs.

decisions.choice: saints (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8.

records.source: Καὶ ἐθαύμασα ἰδὼν αὐτὴν θαῦμα μέγα·
records.gloss: And I marveled having seen her with marvel great.
pieces: The sight of her filled me with great amazement.

L.6: And when I saw her, I marveled with great wonder.

R.6: When I saw her, I was very amazed.

decisions.choice: great wonder: astonishment, not admiration
decisions.reason: John is astounded at what he sees. The same verb is used of the world's wondering at the beast (13:3; 17:8), and the angel's question (17:7) checks any hint of fascination.

records.source: καὶ εἶπέν μοι ὁ ἄγγελος· Διὰ τί ἐθαύμασας;
records.gloss: And said to me the angel: Why did you marvel?
pieces: But the angel said to me, "Why are you amazed?

L.7: And the angel said to me, "Why did you marvel?

R.7: The angel asked me, "Why are you so amazed?

decisions.choice: the angel's explanation begins
decisions.reason: The angel's words run from here to the end of 17:14 and resume at 17:15.

records.source: ἐγὼ ἐρῶ σοι τὸ μυστήριον τῆς γυναικὸς καὶ τοῦ θηρίου τοῦ βαστάζοντος αὐτήν, τοῦ ἔχοντος τὰς ἑπτὰ κεφαλὰς καὶ τὰ δέκα κέρατα·
records.gloss: I will tell you the mystery of the woman and of the beast the carrying her, the having the seven heads and the ten horns.
pieces: Let me tell you the mystery of the woman, and of the beast with the seven heads and ten horns that carries her.

L.7: I will tell you the mystery of the woman and of the beast that carries her, which has the seven heads and the ten horns.

R.7: I will tell you the mystery, the secret meaning, of the woman and of the beast she is riding. It is the beast with seven heads and ten horns.

decisions.choice: the mystery: the meaning of the vision, now explained
decisions.reason: As in 1:20, the angel explains what the symbols stand for. The explanation still uses pictures and needs wisdom (17:9).

decisions.choice: mystery; the secret meaning (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:20.

records.source: τὸ θηρίον ὃ εἶδες ἦν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν, καὶ μέλλει ἀναβαίνειν ἐκ τῆς ἀβύσσου, καὶ εἰς ἀπώλειαν ὑπάγει· καὶ θαυμασθήσονται οἱ κατοικοῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ὧν οὐ γέγραπται τὸ ὄνομα ἐπὶ τὸ βιβλίον τῆς ζωῆς ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου, βλεπόντων τὸ θηρίον ὅτι ἦν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν καὶ παρέσται.
records.gloss: The beast which you saw was and is not, and is about to come up out of the abyss and into destruction goes; and will marvel those dwelling on the earth, of whom not has been written the name on the book of the life from foundation of world, seeing the beast that it was and is not and will be present.
pieces: The beast that you saw existed once and exists no longer; it is going to rise out of the abyss, and it goes on to destruction. The people of the earth, those whose names have not been written in the book of life since the world was founded, will marvel to see the beast, for it was, and is not, and will be present again.

L.8: The beast that you saw was, and is not, and is about to come up out of the abyss and goes to destruction; and those who live on the earth, whose name has not been written in the book of life from the foundation of the world, will marvel when they see the beast, that it was and is not and will be present.

R.8: The beast you saw was alive once, but it is not alive now. It will come up out of the bottomless pit, but then it will be destroyed. The people on earth whose names were not written in the book of life before the world was made will be amazed when they see the beast. It was once alive, it is not alive now, but it will come again.

decisions.choice: was, is not, and will come: a parody of God's name
decisions.reason: God is the one "who is and who was and who is coming" (1:4, 8). The beast "was, and is not, and will come up": it mimics God's eternity and Christ's death and resurrection (13:3, 14), but its coming leads only to destruction.

decisions.choice: the beast that returns: perhaps the legend of Nero
decisions.reason: See the note on 13:3. The language of a ruler who was, is not, and will return may echo the rumors that Nero would come back.

decisions.choice: names not written from the foundation of the world
decisions.reason: See the note on 13:8.

decisions.choice: abyss (L, B); bottomless pit (R)
decisions.reason: As in 9:1.

records.source: Ὧδε ὁ νοῦς ὁ ἔχων σοφίαν.
records.gloss: Here the mind the having wisdom.
pieces: Here a wise mind is needed.

L.9: Here [is] the mind that has wisdom.

R.9: Here you need wisdom to understand.

decisions.choice: a call for wisdom, as in 13:18
decisions.reason: The angel calls for understanding, as John did with the number of the beast. The symbols point to realities the readers can recognize.

records.source: αἱ ἑπτὰ κεφαλαὶ ἑπτὰ ὄρη εἰσίν, ὅπου ἡ γυνὴ κάθηται ἐπ’ αὐτῶν.
records.gloss: The seven heads seven mountains are, where the woman sits on them.
pieces: The seven heads are seven mountains, and the woman is seated on them.

L.9: The seven heads are seven mountains, on which the woman sits.

R.9: The seven heads are seven hills where the woman sits.

decisions.choice: seven mountains: the seven hills of Rome
alternatives: seven kingdoms, since mountains can stand for kingdoms (Jeremiah 51:25; Daniel 2:35)
decisions.reason: Rome was famous as the city on seven hills, and its writers and coins spoke of it so. To John's readers the woman seated on seven hills would most naturally be Rome. The next sentence gives the heads a second meaning, seven kings, so the symbol is not exhausted by geography.

decisions.choice: mountains (L, B); hills (R)
decisions.reason: ὄρη means mountain or hill; Readable uses "hills", the familiar description of Rome.

records.source: καὶ βασιλεῖς ἑπτά εἰσιν·
records.gloss: And kings seven are.
pieces: They are also seven kings.

decisions.choice: a second meaning for the seven heads
decisions.reason: The heads are both seven mountains and seven kings: the symbol has more than one meaning.

records.source: οἱ πέντε ἔπεσαν, ὁ εἷς ἔστιν, ὁ ἄλλος οὔπω ἦλθεν, καὶ ὅταν ἔλθῃ ὀλίγον αὐτὸν δεῖ μεῖναι, καὶ τὸ θηρίον ὃ ἦν καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν.
records.gloss: The five fell, the one is, the other not yet came, and when he comes a little him it is necessary to remain. \v 11 And the beast which was and is not,
pieces: Five of them have fallen; one is now; the other is still to come, and when he does, he must remain only briefly.
And the beast that was and is not

L.10: The five have fallen, the one is, the other has not yet come, and when he comes he must remain a little while.
L.11: And the beast that was and is not,

R.10: Five of these kings have already died. One is ruling now. The last one has not come yet. When he comes, he will rule for only a short time.
R.11: The beast that was alive once and is not alive now

decisions.choice: seven kings: a series of rulers, most of them past
alternatives: seven Roman emperors, counted from Augustus or from Julius Caesar
seven empires (Egypt, Assyria, Babylon, Persia, Greece, Rome, and one to come)
a symbolic seven: the whole line of earthly rulers
decisions.reason: Many have tried to count seven emperors so that the sixth is reigning when John writes, but the count depends on where one starts and whom one includes, and no count fits every detail. Seven may also stand for completeness: the series of earthly powers is almost finished, and the last will be brief.

decisions.choice: the sentence runs on into 17:11
decisions.reason: The source data divides the sentence so that "and the beast that was and is not" closes this record and its predicate, "is itself an eighth", opens the next. The record follows that division.

decisions.choice: the subject left open at the end (L, B, R)
decisions.reason: Every level ends with the subject of 17:11, completed in the next record, as the record division requires (m2).

records.source: καὶ αὐτὸς ὄγδοός ἐστιν καὶ ἐκ τῶν ἑπτά ἐστιν, καὶ εἰς ἀπώλειαν ὑπάγει.
records.gloss: also he an eighth is, and out of the seven is, and into destruction goes.
pieces: is an eighth king, and yet it belongs to the seven, and it is on its way to destruction.

L.11: it is itself also an eighth, and it is of the seven, and it goes to destruction.

R.11: is an eighth king. But it belongs with the seven kings, and it is going to be destroyed.

decisions.choice: an eighth that belongs to the seven
decisions.reason: The beast is a further ruler, an eighth, yet of the same kind as the seven, perhaps one of them returned (17:8). Eight was also the number of new beginnings, and the beast's return parodies resurrection. Whatever it is, its end is destruction.

records.source: καὶ τὰ δέκα κέρατα ἃ εἶδες δέκα βασιλεῖς εἰσιν, οἵτινες βασιλείαν οὔπω ἔλαβον, ἀλλὰ ἐξουσίαν ὡς βασιλεῖς μίαν ὥραν λαμβάνουσιν μετὰ τοῦ θηρίου.
records.gloss: And the ten horns which you saw ten kings are, who a kingdom not yet received, but authority as kings one hour receive with the beast.
pieces: As for the ten horns you saw, they are ten kings who have no kingdom yet; but together with the beast they receive royal authority for one hour.

L.12: And the ten horns that you saw are ten kings, who have not yet received a kingdom, but they receive authority as kings for one hour with the beast.

R.12: The ten horns you saw are ten kings. They have not started to rule yet. But they will rule with the beast for a very short time.

decisions.choice: ten horns, ten kings: Daniel 7:24
decisions.reason: "As for the ten horns, out of this kingdom ten kings shall arise" (Daniel 7:24). "One hour" means a very short time.

records.source: οὗτοι μίαν γνώμην ἔχουσιν, καὶ τὴν δύναμιν καὶ ἐξουσίαν αὐτῶν τῷ θηρίῳ διδόασιν.
records.gloss: These one mind have, and the power and authority of them to the beast they give.
pieces: They are of one mind, and they hand over their power and authority to the beast.

L.13: These have one mind, and they give their power and authority to the beast.

R.13: These kings all agree with each other. They will give their power and authority to the beast.

decisions.choice: one mind: a single purpose
decisions.reason: γνώμην means purpose or intention. They act together in serving the beast, and God uses that very purpose (17:17).

records.source: οὗτοι μετὰ τοῦ ἀρνίου πολεμήσουσιν, καὶ τὸ ἀρνίον νικήσει αὐτούς, ὅτι κύριος κυρίων ἐστὶν καὶ βασιλεὺς βασιλέων, καὶ οἱ μετ’ αὐτοῦ κλητοὶ καὶ ἐκλεκτοὶ καὶ πιστοί.
records.gloss: These with the Lamb will make war, and the Lamb will overcome them, because Lord of lords he is and King of kings, and those with him called and chosen and faithful.
pieces: They will make war on the Lamb, and the Lamb will overcome them, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is Lord of lords and King of kings; and those who are with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} are the called, the chosen, the faithful."

L.14: These will make war with the Lamb, and the Lamb will overcome them, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is Lord of lords and King of kings, and those with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [are] called and chosen and faithful."

R.14: They will fight against the Lamb. But the Lamb will win the victory over them, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the Lord over all lords and the King over all kings. The people with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} are the ones God has called and chosen, and they are faithful to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

decisions.choice: Lord of lords and King of kings
decisions.reason: God is "God of gods and Lord of lords" (Deuteronomy 10:17; compare Daniel 2:47). The Lamb bears the title, and it is written on him in 19:16.

decisions.choice: the called, chosen and faithful share the Lamb's victory
decisions.reason: Those with the Lamb are called and chosen by God and have stayed faithful (compare Matthew 22:14). The battle is described in 19:11-21.

decisions.choice: overcome (L, B); win the victory (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:5.

records.source: Καὶ λέγει μοι· Τὰ ὕδατα ἃ εἶδες, οὗ ἡ πόρνη κάθηται, λαοὶ καὶ ὄχλοι εἰσὶν καὶ ἔθνη καὶ γλῶσσαι.
records.gloss: And he says to me: The waters which you saw, where the prostitute sits, peoples and crowds are and nations and tongues.
pieces: He went on: "The waters you saw, on which the prostitute sits, are peoples and crowds, nations and languages.

L.15: And he says to me, "The waters that you saw, where the prostitute sits, are peoples and crowds and nations and languages.

R.15: Then the angel said to me, "You saw the waters where the prostitute sits. They are the peoples, crowds, nations, and languages of the world.

decisions.choice: waters as peoples
decisions.reason: The prophets compare peoples and armies to floods of water (Isaiah 8:7; 17:12-13; Jeremiah 47:2). The city sits enthroned over many nations.

records.source: καὶ τὰ δέκα κέρατα ἃ εἶδες καὶ τὸ θηρίον, οὗτοι μισήσουσι τὴν πόρνην, καὶ ἠρημωμένην ποιήσουσιν αὐτὴν καὶ γυμνήν, καὶ τὰς σάρκας αὐτῆς φάγονται, καὶ αὐτὴν κατακαύσουσιν ἐν πυρί·
records.gloss: And the ten horns which you saw and the beast, these will hate the prostitute and desolate will make her and naked, and the flesh of her they will eat and her they will burn up with fire.
pieces: The ten horns and the beast that you saw will turn against the prostitute in hatred, leave her ruined and naked, eat her flesh, and burn her up with fire.

L.16: And the ten horns that you saw, and the beast, these will hate the prostitute and will make her desolate and naked, and they will eat her flesh and burn her up with fire.

R.16: The ten horns and the beast you saw will hate the prostitute. They will take everything she has and leave her naked. They will eat her flesh and burn her up with fire.

decisions.choice: her lovers turn on her: Ezekiel 16 and 23
decisions.reason: In Ezekiel the nations with whom unfaithful Jerusalem played the harlot strip her and destroy her (Ezekiel 16:37-41; 23:25-29). Evil turns on itself: the powers that carried the city destroy it.

decisions.choice: a picture of a city's ruin
decisions.reason: The violent images are the prophets' way of describing the fall of a city (compare 18:8-9, where Babylon is burned). They describe God's judgment on a corrupt power and give no license for violence against anyone.

records.source: ὁ γὰρ θεὸς ἔδωκεν εἰς τὰς καρδίας αὐτῶν ποιῆσαι τὴν γνώμην αὐτοῦ, καὶ ποιῆσαι μίαν γνώμην καὶ δοῦναι τὴν βασιλείαν αὐτῶν τῷ θηρίῳ, ἄχρι τελεσθήσονται οἱ λόγοι τοῦ θεοῦ.
records.gloss: For the God gave into the hearts of them to do the purpose of him, and to do one purpose and to give the kingdom of them to the beast, until will be completed the words of the God.
pieces: It is God who has moved their hearts to do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} intends: to act with one mind and to hand their kingdom over to the beast, until God's words have been fulfilled.

L.17: For God has put into their hearts to carry out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} purpose, and to carry out one purpose, and to give their kingdom to the beast, until the words of God are fulfilled.

R.17: God made them want to do what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} planned. So they agreed to give their power to rule to the beast. This will last until everything God has said comes true.

decisions.choice: God uses even the plans of his enemies
decisions.reason: The kings act by their own will, but God has put it in their hearts, so that what they do serves his purpose, as he used Assyria as the rod of his anger (Isaiah 10:5-7). Their alliance with the beast lasts only until God's words are fulfilled.

records.source: καὶ ἡ γυνὴ ἣν εἶδες ἔστιν ἡ πόλις ἡ μεγάλη ἡ ἔχουσα βασιλείαν ἐπὶ τῶν βασιλέων τῆς γῆς.
records.gloss: And the woman which you saw is the city the great the having kingdom over the kings of the earth.
pieces: The woman you saw is the great city, the one that reigns over the kings of the earth."

L.18: And the woman that you saw is the great city that has kingship over the kings of the earth."

R.18: The woman you saw is the great city that rules over the kings of the earth."

decisions.choice: the great city that rules the kings: Rome in John's day, and every such power
decisions.reason: In John's day only Rome ruled over the kings of the earth, and with the seven hills (17:9) the identification would have been plain to his readers. But the city is given a symbolic name, Babylon, and its fall is told in words from the prophets' oracles against Babylon and Tyre: it stands for every power that sets itself against God and his people.
